fixture_name: A9 Ballinluig SB signage/VRS-adjacent visibility — real UK Stage 1&2 RSA (Transport Scotland OGL release)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Observed sight-line obstruction at a high-speed off-slip terminus undermining driver slowing awareness is a genuine safety mechanism squarely within the signage scheme's purpose, not a vacuous observation.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-UK-025 ('Vegetation affects views to end of slip road, reducing driver awareness of requirement to slow'), satisfying the quote requirement beyond mere registry citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under GG 119 Stage 1 semantics, keeping the safety issue distinct from any compliance question and tying it to RSA action tracking rather than design approval.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: a defined drive-through verification at design speed after clearance, with recording in the handover file alongside the agreed RSA action; viable as a staged acceptance check.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are plausibly absent on the slip carriageway itself, and the finding explicitly acknowledges their non-exposure while scoping road users to vehicle occupants, meeting the acknowledged-not-applicable bar.
